passage:
Class note, couples' evening at the community hall. After last week's role-play, Vandana and her husband came back and told the group how it went when his parents visited. Before the visit they had agreed on two things: their salaries and the flat's plans stay between the two of them, and Sunday lunch is always open to the family. When the father-in-law asked about money, Vandana smiled and said, “That's ours to keep, Papa-ji, but we would love your advice on the kitchen.” Nobody raised a voice. Papa-ji laughed and asked for tea instead. The mother-in-law, at first stiff, was showing the couple her recipe book by evening. I asked the group what they had noticed.
Alka, class tutor

qa.q: What two things did Vandana and her husband agree on before the visit?
qa.a: They agreed that their salaries and the flat's plans stay between the two of them, and that Sunday lunch is open to the family.

qa.q: Why did Vandana add, “we would love your advice on the kitchen”?
qa.a: Vandana seems to want the refusal to feel warm and not like a wall, so she offers something the father-in-law can share in.

qa.q: What did the couple do that helped the boundary be accepted?
qa.a: They decided together beforehand, communicated kindly and gave the family a clear way to belong, so nobody felt shut out.

qa.q: How might the mother-in-law have felt by evening?
qa.a: The mother-in-law seems to have relaxed and felt included, since she was stiff at first and then showed the couple her recipe book.

grounding: A young couple agrees on what to share and what to keep private, then says so kindly to the in-laws, and the boundary is accepted.

passage:
Gurpreet's diary, Saturday night.
My husband Jomon and I sat on the balcony before his parents arrived and settled it: we will tell them about the housewarming, but not about how much rent we pay or what we saved. I practised the sentence three times. When his mother asked at lunch how much the flat costs, my hands went cold. I said, “Mummy-ji, that part we're keeping between us, but you are the first two we are inviting.” The room went still. His father put down the spoon. Then his mother said, “Achha, so which day?” and passed me the pickle. My heart is still pounding. Jomon squeezed my hand under the table. I think it went well.

qa.q: How many times did Gurpreet practise the sentence?
qa.a: Gurpreet practised the sentence three times.

qa.q: What was Gurpreet feeling when the flat's cost was asked about at lunch?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt nervous, with cold hands, and still spoke warmly. The pounding heart afterwards shows the strain. 😰

qa.q: What made the boundary easier to accept at that lunch?
qa.a: The couple had agreed together beforehand what to share and what to keep private, and Gurpreet added a warm invitation so the refusal did not feel like rejection.

qa.q: How might Jomon's mother have taken the words, “that part we're keeping between us”?
qa.a: She seems to have accepted it, since after the room went still she asked, “Achha, so which day?” and passed the pickle.

grounding: A young couple decides together what they will share and keep private and tells the in-laws kindly, and the boundary is accepted.

passage:
Sahil: Mummy just asked in the family group for our money details again 😅
Charu: Okay. Before we reply, what are we comfortable sharing?
Sahil: That we're doing fine. Not numbers.
Charu: Agreed. And the house-hunting? I'd rather tell them once we've decided.
Sahil: Same. I'll write it, you check?
Charu: Yes. Keep it warm, she means well.
[Family group]
Sahil: Mummy, we love that you care 🙂 We've decided to keep money details between the two of us, but we're managing well, promise. We'll share big news, like a house, as soon as it's final.
Mummy: Hmm. Okay beta. Just worried.
Papa: Sensible.
Bua: Our children are growing up!
[Private chat]
Charu: That went better than I thought 🙏

qa.q: Who wrote the reply in the family group?
qa.a: Sahil wrote it, and Charu checked it.

qa.q: How did Charu feel after the family replied?
qa.a: Charu felt relieved and pleasantly surprised, saying it went better than expected.

qa.q: Which part of how Sahil and Charu handled this worked, and why?
qa.a: Agreeing privately first on what to share, then replying warmly with reassurance; the kind tone made the limit easier to accept.

qa.q: How might Mummy feel reading Sahil's message?
qa.a: She is a little let down and still worried ('Hmm... Just worried'), but the warm tone helps her accept it.

grounding: A young couple agrees together on what to keep private from family and says it kindly, and the family accepts it.

passage: In Tarun's family house in a small town near Hubballi, doors were never shut. Amma walked into the young couple's room to fold clothes, Atte came in to borrow the mirror, and the nephews ran in at six in the morning. Charu never complained aloud, but she had started changing in the bathroom. One night, Tarun and Charu sat on the terrace and decided together: their room would stay theirs in the evenings and early mornings, and the rest of the house was open to everyone. The next day, Tarun brought Amma a string of jasmine and said, 'Amma, we love that everyone drops in. Can we ask for a knock before eight in the morning and after dinner? It'll help us rest.' Amma laughed, a little hurt. 'In my time, who knocked?' But that evening, there was a soft tap on the door.

qa.q: What did Tarun bring Amma the next day?
qa.a: A string of jasmine.

qa.q: What does Charu changing in the bathroom suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable and short of privacy with people walking in, even though she never complained aloud.

qa.q: Which step made the request easier for Amma to accept?
qa.a: Deciding together first and then asking warmly, with jasmine and appreciation for the drop-ins, instead of complaining in anger.

qa.q: How might Amma experience the request?
qa.a: She feels a little hurt, since in her time nobody knocked, but she respects it and taps on the door that evening.

grounding: A young couple agrees together on a privacy limit in a joint household and asks for it warmly, and it is accepted.

subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
passage: Diego's mother, Carmen, had a spare key to their flat in Valencia, and she used it. Twice a week, Tuan came home from his shift to find the fridge restocked, his shirts ironed and the sofa cushions rearranged. He was grateful and also quietly worn out. One Sunday, over coffee, Tuan told Diego how it felt, and Diego admitted he'd been avoiding the subject. They agreed on what they wanted: Carmen keeps the key for emergencies, and she calls before visiting. At the next family lunch, Diego took his mother's hand. 'Mamá, we love your cooking and your help. Please keep the key, but call first, so we can be home and actually sit with you.' Carmen blinked, then laughed. 'So now I need an appointment?' Diego's father said, 'We did the same with my mother.' The next Tuesday, she called.

qa.q: What did Tuan find when coming home twice a week?
qa.a: The fridge restocked, his shirts ironed and the sofa cushions rearranged.

qa.q: How did Tuan feel about Carmen's visits?
qa.a: He was grateful and also quietly worn out, with no say over when she came.

qa.q: What made Diego's request likely to be accepted?
qa.a: The couple agreed privately first, and Diego asked warmly, thanking Carmen and letting her keep the key, only asking her to call first.

qa.q: Why might Diego's father react as he did?
qa.a: He had set a similar limit with his own mother, so he sees the request as normal and helps Carmen accept it.

grounding: A couple agrees together on a boundary about visits and offers it to a parent with warmth, and it is accepted.

subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
passage: The clinic waiting room smelled of sanitiser and old magazines. Bhavna's phone buzzed again: the family group, where Ujjwal's father Santosh had written, "Send the full report when it comes." Ujjwal's mother added folded hands; his aunt added three. Last month Bhavna had replied sharply, "It's my body, not a group project," and the chat had gone silent for a week. Now she turned the screen towards Ujjwal. "Same rule we agreed at home?" she asked. "Routine things stay with us. Anything serious, we tell them ourselves." He nodded and stepped into the corridor to call. "Papa, thank you for caring so much. The small check-ups we'll keep between us two. If anything ever needs you, you'll hear it from me first, promise." A pause. Then Santosh laughed. "Okay, okay. Just tell me she's smiling." Through the glass, Bhavna was.

qa.q: Who wrote "Send the full report when it comes" in the family group?
qa.a: Ujjwal's father Santosh wrote it in the family group.

qa.q: What might Bhavna have been worried about when she turned the screen towards Ujjwal?
qa.a: She was probably uneasy about another week of cold silence like last month, and wanted to feel sure they still agreed before anyone replied.

qa.q: Why did this attempt work better than Bhavna's reply last month?
qa.a: The couple had agreed on the rule together first, and Ujjwal gave it warmly, with thanks and a promise, so it sounded like care rather than rejection.

qa.q: How does Santosh probably see the phone call?
qa.a: He may feel a little shut out at first, but the thanks and the promise let him accept the limit with a laugh and still feel included.

grounding: Shows a young couple agreeing together what stays private from Ujjwal's parents and saying it kindly, so the boundary is accepted.
